{{Top}}
{{Quote|Our new Oversectors are comprised of many smaller sectors. This structure allows for direct command of military forces, control of information, and more efficient taxation of Imperial subjects.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Wullf Yularen/Legends|Wullf Yularen]], ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''|<ref name="Imperial Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>}}
[[File:Clone_Wars_Sector_Armies.png|thumb|right|250px|The original twenty Oversectors at the start of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Their boundaries would be substantially reformed in later years.]]
An '''Oversector''', also called a '''Priority Sector''', was an area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]] comprising many [[Sector/Legends|sectors]] or parts of sectors plagued with [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] activity.

==History==
The oversectors were originally created during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] by the [[Sector Governance Decree/Legends|Sector Governance Decree]]. The decree gave twenty of the new Moffs responsibility for supporting the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic's]] twenty [[Sector Army/Legends|Sector Armies]]. These Moffs' military territories, the oversectors, matched the Sector Armies' theaters of operations. They crossed the boundaries of the regional sectors and freed their Moffs from having to constantly consult local authorities.<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

After the [[Declaration of a New Order]], oversectors were reorganized as part of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] militarization recommended by the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]], with each oversector composed of a number between dozens or hundreds of smaller sectors. According to the field manual for the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]], ''[[Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]'', the redistricting of the Imperial territory allowed for increased efficiency, namely for direct command of military operations, control of information, as well as more efficient taxation of various Imperial subjects, as well as ensuring that the politicians back the actions of the military to avoid being pulled in competing directions. In addition, it was also explained that part of the reason for their redistricting was to further divorce the Empire from the Old Republic, as the latter divided the galaxy into thousands of sectors, each representing a senator which created chaos.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" /> The new oversectors usually contained between two and a dozen sectors. The [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moffs]] were assigned by [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] as a military Regional Governors, superseding the authority of Sectorial Governors ([[Moff/Legends|Moffs]]), [[Planetary Governor/Legends|Planetary Governors]], and other local authorities. The Grand Moffs were given direct control over the systems within their Oversectors, and could use practically limitless resources and means to squash Rebel activity therein, with the military allotments also being tailored to be appropriate to his station. Some of the original oversectors remained unchanged (such as the [[Imperial Center Oversector|Coruscant Oversector]]) or were expanded, and several others disappeared: the [[Greater Seswenna/Legends|Greater Seswenna]] oversector, originally surrounding [[Eriadu/Legends|Eriadu]], came to encompass almost the entirety of the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]], with the exception of elements of the [[Quelii Oversector|Quelii]] and [[Bright Jewel Oversector/Legends|Bright Jewel Oversectors]].<ref name="TEA" />

Oversectors were sometimes known as priority sectors. This term was applied to areas where the Empire was pursuing active military campaigns or special military projects. The [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] Project was considered as a priority sector.<ref name="TEA" />

Although oversector control by Grand Moffs was intended to be such that the Grand Moffs would "not think twice" about crossing sector borders, as well as having no need to consult local politicians concerning the actions of the Empire specifically to ensure [[hit-and-hype raiding]] could not be used, it was ultimately flawed in implementation, which was exploited by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] by staging raids at the border of an oversector and then ensuring that the Grand Moffs enter a turf war, which [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] noted.<ref name="Imperial Handbook" />
